title: Supplier Payment Terms, Budget Tiering, and Approval Patterns
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview:

This document defines standardized patterns for supplier payment terms, ties procurement approval tiers to budget ownership, and prescribes authorization steps to reduce fiscal risk. It is intended for finance, procurement leads, purchasing approvers, and partnering engineering/product teams who request supplier commitments.

Purpose:
- Reduce invoice disputes and late-payment costs by standardizing payment term negotiations.
- Ensure budget accountability by mapping approval tiers to specific budget owners and forecast windows.
- Provide a clear, auditable purchase and payment workflow for obligations that impact revenue recognition or multi-month commitments.

Scope:
- Applies to all vendor agreements, purchase orders (POs), subscriptions, and capacity commitments with total expected spend > $5,000 annualized.
- Excludes petty cash, corporate card purchases under $1,000, and pre-approved SaaS subscriptions with centralized subscriptions program.

Key Principles:
1) Budget-first: No commitment is valid until associated budget is confirmed for the fiscal period (capex or opex).
2) Tiered approvals: Higher fiscal impact requires broader review (procurement + finance partner + legal for contract language).
3) Standard terms default: Use standard Redwood payment terms and amendments only with finance approval.
4) Clear ownership: Each PO must list a Budget Owner (name + cost center) and a Contract Owner.

Standard Payment Terms (default):
- Net 30 (preferred) for US and EU suppliers.
- Net 14 for one-time consultants and contractors where earlier payment accelerates delivery and vendor discounts apply.
- Net 45 only if vendor provides at least 2% discount for early payment or extended delivery milestones justify the timing.
- Prepayment (up to 50%) permitted only for hardware/on-prem installs with explicit milestone schedule and finance escrow account.

Decision Matrix: budget tiers and required approvers

| Fiscal Impact (Annualized) | Approval Chain (order) | Procurement Steps | Contracts Review |
|---------------------------:|------------------------|-------------------|-----------------|
| $1k - $5k                 | Requestor -> Manager   | Create PO -> Procurement review optional | No legal review |
| $5k - $50k                | Requestor -> Manager -> Budget Owner -> Procurement | Mandatory PO -> Procurement negotiates terms | Legal review if custom T&Cs |
| $50k - $250k             | Requestor -> Manager -> Finance Partner -> Procurement Head | Sourcing process, multiple quotes recommended | Legal review required; commercial team notified |
| > $250k                  | Requestor -> Manager -> Finance Director -> VP/Head of Business Unit -> CFO sign-off | Executive sourcing, vendor risk review, finance modeling | Legal + Security + Compliance sign-off |

Note: For Dedicated Capacity contracts and multi-year commitments, use the >$250k flow regardless of annualized amount.

Procedural Steps (numbered):
1. Requestor fills the procurement intake form with justification, deliverables, and preferred payment schedule. Include estimated annualized cost and budget center.
2. Manager approves and confirms there is a product/engineering or go-to-market need.
3. Budget Owner verifies available forecast capacity for the relevant fiscal window and either confirms budget or proposes a reforecast.
4. Procurement validates vendor: financial stability, sanctions check, payment currency, and collects at least one certificate of insurance for professional services > $25k.
5. Procurement negotiates standard payment terms. Any deviation requires documented finance sign-off with reason.
6. If required by tier, Legal reviews terms and negotiates liability/indemnity/CIP/KMS clauses.
7. PO issued, vendor acknowledges, and Service Commencement Date (SCD) is recorded in PO metadata.
8. For multi-period or subscription deals, schedule quarterly budget reviews and automated usage metering to feed the committed spend into rolling forecasts.

Table: Approval thresholds (concise)

| Threshold | Minimum Approvers | Additional Controls |
|----------:|------------------|---------------------|
| <$5k     | Manager          | Standard vendor check |
| $5k–$50k | Manager, Budget Owner | PO required; procurement notified |
| $50k–$250k | Finance Partner, Procurement Head | 2 vendor quotes; legal review if custom terms |
| >$250k   | Finance Director, BU VP, CFO | Executive approval; board notification if strategic multi-year |

Default Contract Clauses (checklist to include in SOW/PO):
- Scope, deliverables, acceptance criteria, termination for convenience (30–60 days), SLAs if applicable, IP assignment for custom work, data handling and residency clauses, indemnity caps aligned to budget tier, audit rights (for >$50k), and payment schedule tied to milestones.

PO Template (JSON example to paste into the procurement system):

```json
{
  "po_number": "AUTO-GEN",
  "vendor": "<vendor_name>",
  "amount": "<annualized_amount>",
  "currency": "USD",
  "budget_owner": "Name (Cost center)",
  "contract_owner": "Name (email)",
  "payment_terms": "Net 30",
  "service_commencement": "YYYY-MM-DD",
  "notes": "Attach SOW and security questionnaire link",
  "approvals": ["manager_approval_id", "budget_owner_id"]
}
```

Exceptions and Escalation:
- If a supplier requires non-standard payment terms (e.g., Net 90), procurement must run a cost-of-capital calculation and obtain Finance Director approval.
- Emergency procurements (urgent infra/hardware to restore production) may be escalated to SRE + Procurement Head; documented after-action PO must be created within 5 business days.

Budgeting and Forecast Implications:
- All POs with multi-month impact must be mapped to monthly forecast lines. Procurement will add committed spend to the rolling 12-month forecast during the weekly forecast refresh.
- For Dedicated Capacity contracts, finance will create a committed capacity ledger entry and amortize cost across recognized months in the forecast model.

Metrics and Reporting (monthly cadence):
- % of POs issued with standard payment terms (target: >= 90%).
- Average days-payable outstanding for non-enterprise vendors (target: 28–32 days).
- Number of budget reforecasts triggered by procurement (>5% of BU forecast).
- Number of exceptions requiring executive sign-off.

Owner and RACI (single-line entries):
- Procurement: process owner and vendor diligence (R/A).
- Finance Partner: budget verification and forecasting (R).
- Legal: contract review for custom terms (C).
- Requestor (Product/Eng): requirements and acceptance (I).

Rollout and Training Plan:
1) Week 1–2: Communicate new patterns and thresholds to all BU finance partners and procurement sprints channel.
2) Week 3–4: Training sessions for managers and requestors (recordings uploaded).
3) Week 5–ongoing: Start enforcing PO gates at the procurement system for thresholds above $5k; collect feedback and adjust.

Appendix A — Example scenarios:
- Example 1 (SaaS seat renewal, $42k/year): Requestor submits renewal. Manager approves. Budget Owner confirms opex capacity. Procurement negotiates Net 30 and discount. PO executed with standard SOW. No legal review required.
- Example 2 (On-prem hardware, $320k one-time): Enterprise procurement flow initiated. Finance models capex vs opex impact. Legal and Security run concurrent reviews. Executive sign-off obtained. Payment: 30% deposit (escrowed), remainder by milestones.

Appendix B — Quick checklist for requestors (bulleted):
- Attach business justification and desired start date.
- Identify budget owner, cost center, and GL code if known.
- Attach vendor tax and payment instructions, W-9/EU VAT if applicable.
- Indicate whether vendor requires any special security or residency terms.
